assignment: asg-2026-09-11-A2-deepseek-flash-20-29 (synthetic dry-run only, no model calls)
claims_not_made: no claim about real model behaviour: proposers are synthetic placeholders
no swarm-advantage claim; the harness only makes such a claim checkable
no A2 completion claim; this is a draft for lead-audit and G-AUDIT
no universal scalar score is produced

analysis.model: beta-binomial (or binomial GLMM) with a task random intercept; arm fixed effect; seed as replicates
analysis.multiplicity: Holm across the four planned contrasts

power_analysis.method: two-sided two-proportion normal approximation, alpha=0.05, power=0.80, n=8 per arm
power_analysis.warning: n=8 cannot detect the +3% effect size seen in the offline lab; a 15-point absolute difference needs roughly 60-70 outputs per arm. Sequential extension or more seeds is the only honest fix; lowering the bar is not.

analysis.reporting: per-arm mean +/- sd and best-of-k separately; never a bare max

arms.composition: single strong proposer, effort=high, one sample per task, no communication, no coordinator
arms.label: one strong model

arms.composition: same strong proposer, k independent samples per task, union of candidates passed through the same verifier gate; no cross-agent messaging
arms.label: self-consistency

arms.composition: m DeepSeek Flash agents, one sample per task each, no coordinator, no dead-end channel, no reassignment
arms.label: independent cheap agents

arms.composition: same m cheap agents plus a coordinator that assigns class-bound task cards, enforces the artifact gate, broadcasts refuted regions (dead ends), and reallocates calls by marginal information gain
arms.label: cheap agents + coordinator

arms.composition: iid random selection from the task's candidate pool at the same token spend, plus a shuffled-gate control at the observed base rate
arms.label: matched-budget null
arms.role: mandatory control; the run is uninterpretable without it

artifacts.raw_runs: evaluation/runs/ (created only when execution is unblocked)

config.author: lead-audit

budget_matching.accounting_source: provider usage fields only; estimated tokens are a hard failure (HF-08)
budget_matching.rule: All arms receive the same total completion-token budget B (+/-2%) and the same wall-clock envelope T (+/-2%), enforced by a scheduler that stops an arm when either is exhausted. Verifier calls per accepted artifact and human-review minutes are also equalised.
budget_matching.secondary_diagnostic: an equal-call variant may be run, but it is labelled non-primary and may never be used for a swarm-advantage claim
budget_matching.token_cost_assumption: From framework/pool.py and the measurements in HANDOFF.md: high effort ~12,842 completion tokens/call and low effort ~2,137 on the same prompt, so matching call counts would silently convert the effort axis into the depth axis (HF-11). Calls are therefore reported, not matched.

design.pre_registration: this file is hashed before execution; any change is a versioned amendment with a reason
design.randomization: arm order within a block randomized; adjudicators blind to arm identity
design.seeds_reason: HANDOFF process rule: max-statistics over fewer than 8 seeds have already produced two retracted readings in this project. With 8 seeds, best-of-k is reported separately from mean-of-k and never as the headline (HF-09).
design.stopping_rule: Fixed-horizon primary analysis at 8 seeds. An optional sequential extension uses O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending with 3 looks; no peeking outside the spending plan.
design.unit_of_analysis: one task x one arm x one seed

endpoints.decision_rule: (1) apply the hard-failure guardrail; (2) compare the primary endpoint against the NULL arm's spread; (3) only then rank the surviving arms, and report ties as ties.

guardrail.name: hard_failure_rate
guardrail.rule: if an arm's critical hard-failure rate exceeds 0.10, its accepted count is truncated at the gate for that arm and the arm is flagged; hard failures dominate any primary gain

hypotheses.falsifier: ICC - IC <= 0, or the difference lies inside the NULL spread
hypotheses.statement: ICC - IC > 0 on the primary endpoint, 95% CI excluding 0 and exceeding the NULL spread
S >= ICC on the primary endpoint: at matched tokens, one strong model is not beaten by cheap breadth even with a coordinator
SC > S: sampling beats single-shot at matched tokens

hypotheses.falsifier: any arm pair outside tolerance -> the comparison is void (HF-11)
hypotheses.statement: all arms matched within 2% on tokens and wall-clock

endpoints.no_universal_scalar_score: TRUE by construction. The report is a gate + a primary endpoint + a Pareto table of secondary metrics. There is no weighted composite.

primary.definition: (number of task outputs that pass their task gate AND an independent blind adjudication) / (total completion tokens / 1e6)
primary.name: accepted_artifacts_per_1M_tokens

secondary.duplication: 1 - mean pairwise novelty; Kish ESS for reviewers, never nominal n

secondary.per_class_coverage: all four frozen classes must be represented or the coverage claim is scoped to the represented subset

execution_status.blocker: no provider config at ~/.maso/model-providers.yaml and no SWARM_PROVIDERS env var in this environment; framework/pool.py cannot construct a Pool
execution_status.what_is_done: design, budget arithmetic, power analysis, synthetic dry-run of the full metrics pipeline, negative control on budget matching
execution_status.what_is_not_done: any real arm execution; no result is claimed

falsifier_of_this_design: arms not matched within 2% on tokens and wall-clock
primary endpoint replaced by a universal scalar score
no NULL arm, or the NULL arm given a different budget
an arm's outputs adjudicated by their author
config.question: At matched token and wall-clock budget, does a cheap-agent swarm with a coordinator produce more gate-accepted, non-duplicated, citation-supported artifacts per token than (a) one strong model, (b) self-consistency on the same strong model, or (c) the same cheap agents without a coordinator?

tasks.difficulty_control: the same task set and the same order for every arm; per-task random intercept in the analysis
tasks.suite: 24 auto-gradable or adjudicated micro-tasks drawn from the frozen class work, 6 of each type

types.gold: the unmutated schema plus the injected-mutation label
types.name: class-binding repair
types.prompt: given a mutated formulation schema, repair it to satisfy rule_spec R01-R16

types.name: citation binding
types.prompt: given a claim and N candidate sources, select the source whose physical scope matches the class

types.gate: checklist: finite witness, genericity clause, class-correct family, machine-checkable steps
types.name: falsifier construction
types.prompt: write a tier-1 falsifier for a named class

types.gate: exact match to L1 registry fields
types.gold: ledger source_meta once L1 completes it
types.name: scope extraction
types.prompt: extract matter_model, Lambda, dimension, symmetry, formulation from a primary-source abstract

traps_encoded: token budget equalised across effort, not call count (HANDOFF: 6x cost difference)
empty / truncated / timeout counted separately and never as 'no answer'
evaluator runs behind a process boundary with a hard timeout (no in-process arbitrary code)
gateway concurrency capped at 16 (measured: 24 -> 2 failures, 32 -> 15 failures)
driver scripts carry an __main__ guard (macOS spawn)
verifier cost counted in the budget

limitations: token matching forces fewer, more expensive episodes for multi-sample arms, so between-arm rates are computed over different episode prefixes; episodes_attempted and per-class coverage are reported so the confound stays visible
synthetic model parameters are placeholders and carry no information about real models
the iid null arm exhausts the episode suite before its token budget, so its consumption is not token-matched; it is a control, never a primary arm
violates: no metric is combined into a single score; each arm reports the same metric set
